title: A Reluctant Rise In EV Prices

A Reluctant Rise In EV Prices

Ernan Cui

Gavekal Dragonomics | 22 Sep 2026

Is China’s legendary price war in electric vehicles finally over? After nearly three years of steady declines in prices, all major automakers have raised prices in recent months. The average price of EVs sold in August was around RMB178,000, up from around RMB168,000 a year ago and roughly back to where it was in the middle of 2024. On the surface, that’s exactly what the government has been trying to achieve with its successive and increasingly intrusive interventions into what it calls destructive “involutionary” competition in the sector. But today’s higher prices are not translating into more sustainable profits for EV makers, because they are the result of higher costs rather than reduced competition. More worryingly, higher prices risk turning into another headwind for sales at a time when households are already reducing purchases of EVs.EV prices started falling in early 2023, when market leaders Tesla and BYD celebrated the reopening from Covid with big price cuts aimed at boosting their market share. Other automakers soon followed. Falling battery prices and continuous improvements in production technology enabled intense competition to see who could offer the most features at the lowest price, and consumers came to expect ever-cheaper EVs. The falling prices squeezed margins for producers but did not trigger significant consolidation in the industry.
